claims: The Artemis II crew safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The Artemis II splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Orion spacecraft named "Integrity" completed a 10-day mission.
The Orion spacecraft landed roughly 60 miles off the San Diego coast.
The Orion spacecraft landed for recovery by the U.S. Navy.
The Artemis II splashdown occurred in the Pacific Ocean approximately 50-60 nautical miles off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II splashdown occurred on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The U.S. Navy ship USS John P. Murtha was positioned to recover the Artemis II crew.
The capsule performed a "skip entry" technique to manage heat and reduce landing loads.
After landing, the capsule inflated five orange airbags.
The five orange airbags turned the spacecraft into an upright position for astronaut exit.
Artemis I splashed down on December 11, 2022.
Artemis I splashed down in the Pacific Ocean near Guadalupe Island.
